title: Effects of nonlocal interactions on s- and d-wave superconducting correlations in the extended Hubbard model
abstract: We investigate the influence of nonlocal interactions on superconducting correlations within the extended Hubbard model. In addition to the on-site Coulomb interaction and nearest-neighbor hopping, we include next-nearest-neighbor hopping together with several physically relevant nonlocal terms, namely nearest-neighbor Coulomb interaction, correlated hopping, exchange interaction, and pair hopping. Using Lanczos exact diagonalization on a $4\times4$ cluster, supported by projector quantum Monte Carlo simulations for selected parameter regimes, we analyze pairing correlations in both the s- and d-wave channels. We demonstrate that nonlocal interactions exert a highly nontrivial and symmetry-dependent influence on superconducting correlations. While the on-site repulsion in cooperation with next-nearest-neighbor hopping enhances d-wave pairing tendencies, correlated hopping and nearest-neighbor Coulomb interaction strongly promote s-wave correlations, whereas exchange and pair-hopping interactions can efficiently suppress superconductivity beyond relatively small critical strengths. When all nonlocal interactions are considered simultaneously, the resulting phase diagrams reveal a complex interplay and competition between different pairing symmetries. Our results highlight the crucial role of extended interactions in shaping the pairing landscape of strongly correlated systems and demonstrate that a comprehensive treatment beyond the minimal Hubbard model is essential for a realistic description of unconventional superconductivity.
summary: This paper theoretically explores unconventional superconductivity in the extended Hubbard model by incorporating multiple nonlocal interactions. Using exact diagonalization and PQMC, the authors demonstrate that these interactions dictate a complex interplay between s-wave and d-wave pairing symmetries. The findings emphasize that realistic descriptions of strongly correlated materials require going significantly beyond the minimal Hubbard Hamiltonian.
main_problem: The study investigates how various nonlocal interactions influence superconducting correlations (s-wave and d-wave) within the extended Hubbard model.
main_result: Nonlocal interactions have a highly nontrivial, symmetry-dependent effect: $t_n$ enhances d-wave pairing with on-site repulsion, while correlated hopping ($t_c$) strongly promotes s-wave correlations.
method: The research employs Lanczos exact diagonalization on small clusters and supplements results using Projector Quantum Monte Carlo simulations to analyze pair correlation functions.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by the extended Hubbard model, incorporating terms for nearest/next-nearest neighbor hopping ($t, t_n$), on-site repulsion ($U$), and several nonlocal interactions like nearest-neighbor Coulomb interaction ($V$), correlated hopping ($t_c$), exchange ($J$), and pair hopping ($J_c$).
key_observables: Equal-time pair–pair correlation functions for s-wave ($C_s$) and d-wave ($C_d$) symmetries, as well as vertex correlation functions.
important_parameters: Interaction strengths $U, V, t_c, J, J_c$, hopping amplitudes $t, t_n$. The analysis explores regimes where these terms are varied relative to each other.
main_assumptions: The primary limitations include the small system size accessible via exact diagonalization ($4	imes 4$ cluster), though PQMC helps extend the regime of study. It assumes that a comprehensive treatment beyond the minimal Hubbard model is necessary for realism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of $C_s$ and $C_d$ on various parameters (e.g., $U, t_n, J_c$), showing non-monotonic behavior, enhancement, or suppression based on the specific interaction term being varied.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the effect of each nonlocal interaction term ($V, t_c, J, J_c$) individually on pairing correlations. It culminates by examining the combined effects of all interactions to map out a complex phase diagram showing competition between symmetries.
why_interesting: This work provides detailed theoretical insight into how extending the Hubbard model with realistic nonlocal terms can fundamentally alter the predicted superconducting pairing symmetry and strength, which is crucial for understanding high-Tc superconductors.
